headline: All seven majors underwater on their 200-day lines; momentum flat to negative; whales moving Bitcoin off exchanges while stablecoin reserves shrink.
paragraphs: The regime is decisively bearish across the board. Bitcoin trades at 63,653, down 49 percent from its 12-month high of 124,773, and sits below the 200-day moving average. Ethereum at 1,904 is 60.6 percent off its 12-month peak of 4,829, also below the 200-day line. Solana, XRP, Cardano, Binance Coin, and Dogecoin are all positioned identically: below their 200-day averages with no golden crosses in sight. The entire cohort is in a downtrend with no major recovery structure in place. Bitcoin dominance stands at 56.6 percent, holding steady, and total market cap sits at 2.29 trillion, up 0.7 percent on the day but without the technical foundation to support sustained momentum.

Momentum offers little relief. Bitcoin's RSI-14 at 47.4 sits in neutral territory, and its MACD is below signal, indicating the downtrend lacks internal acceleration. Ethereum's RSI at 56.3 is higher but its MACD is also below signal. Across the six other assets, five have MACD below signal and RSI readings in the 40s and low 50s, the realm of neither oversold nor overbought. Only Binance Coin and Dogecoin show MACD above signal, but both trade below their 200-day lines anyway, so momentum gains lack regime support. The picture is one of stalled movement within a downtrend, not a reversal beginning to form.

Derivatives positioning reveals crowding in a weak market. Bitcoin funding at 0.0052 percent per 8 hours (5.7 percent annualized) is positive, meaning longs are paying shorts to hold positions. With 2.02 billion dollars of open interest and a long-to-short ratio of 1.27, Bitcoin perps carry a structural bullish tilt, yet the cash price keeps declining. Ethereum funding is even more aggressive at 0.0072 percent per 8 hours (7.9 percent annualized), with 1.3 billion in open interest and a 1.69 long-to-short ratio. Dogecoin is the outlier: 11 percent annualized funding with a 5.03 long-to-short ratio on only 78.8 million open interest, a highly compressed and expensive setup. XRP, the contrarian, shows negative 0.0083 percent 8-hour funding (minus 9.1 percent annualized), a signal that shorts are paying, yet its long-to-short ratio is 3.28. Liquidations in the last 24 hours totaled 929 on Bitcoin (mostly shorts at 7.67 million), 1,585 on Ethereum (shorts at 11.1 million), and smaller numbers on the alts. The market is paying a high price to stay long, and leverage is tilted that way across the board, a positioning that grows fragile when price rolls over.

Whale and stablecoin flows present a contradiction worth naming. Over the last 24 hours, 230.6 million dollars of Bitcoin moved off exchanges, with outflows of 299.9 million and inflows of 69.3 million. This is the gesture of accumulation into self-custody. Simultaneously, however, stablecoin reserves shrunk 1.16 percent over the last 30 days, down to 305.9 billion, suggesting dry powder is being deployed or drained. The weekly whale flows tell the real story: the past two weeks saw cumulative outflows of 1.08 billion and 1.12 billion (moving off exchanges), but the two weeks before that showed inflows of 147.9 million and 86.6 million back onto them. The recent pattern reversed sharply. Meanwhile, USDT moved 499.7 million onto Binance even as 499.6 million left Binance; at Bitfinex, 169.9 million moved on and 199.9 million moved off. These are round numbers and stablecoin movements, liquidity reshuffling rather than conviction directional flows.

Sentiment sits at 27, firmly in fear territory, within a 30-day range of 20 to 33. The crowd is scared, which is textbook. However, the tape shows no synchronized accumulation: Bitcoin ETF flows on 05 Aug were just 2.8 million inflow (against 352.1 million over the last five sessions), and Ethereum had 53.1 million inflow on 04 Aug but only 30.1 million net over the last five. Both are shallow readings. Bitcoin's 7-day and 30-day price changes are negative at 1.59 percent and 2.97 percent, and spot moves have been orderly downward, not panicked. ETH has actually gained 1.81 percent in 7 days and 6.36 percent in 30 days, a divergence from Bitcoin and the rest of the majors, yet ETH remains deeply underwater and offers no trend reversal signal.

Watch for three conditions to signal a change. First, the 200-day reclaim: if any of the majors, especially Bitcoin or Ethereum, move back above the 200-day moving average and hold, regime confirmation flips. Second, a sustainable reversal in funding: positive funding suggests longs are paying, and if that inverts to negative across the board with price still falling, the crowded long position will have flushed. Third, stablecoin reserve rebuilding: if the dry powder count starts climbing again alongside whale flows, the machinery for a sustained rally is being assembled. None of those conditions are met today. The tape shows a downtrend with no structural support, expensive long leverage, and a crowd that is afraid but not yet capitulating.
